Smith, J. "The impact of social media on mental health." Journal of Psychology 3.1 (2021): 45-58.

Smith, J. "The impact of social media on mental health." Journal of Psychology 3(1) (2021): 45-58.

Last name, Initials. "Title of the paper." Journal Title, vol. number, no. issue (year), page range.

Smith, J. "The impact of social media on mental health." Journal of Psychology 3(1) (2021): 45-58.

ori_prompt:
Write a simple guide for uploading the bibliography database
 on Overleaf.
rmepo_prompt: Create a detailed step-by-step guide specifically for importing and managing a bibliography database within the Overleaf platform, ensuring clarity and precision in each instruction.
rmepo_response:
1. Create a new document in Overleaf:
* Log in to your Overleaf account and create a new document by clicking on the "New Document" button.
* Choose the appropriate template for your document and click "Create".
1. Install bibliography management software:
* In Overleaf, click on the "Settings" button in the top right corner of the screen.
* Scroll down to the "Manage Add-ons" section and click on the "Install" button.
* Search for "BibTeX" and click on the "Install" button.
* Once the installation is complete, click on the "Close and return to Overleaf" button.
1. Create a BibTeX file:
* In Overleaf, click on the "Bibliography" button in the top menu bar.
* Choose the appropriate citation style for your document (e.g. APA, MLA, etc.).
* Click on the "Create Bibliography" button.
* In the BibTeX file, create a new entry for each source you want to cite in your document.
* Each entry should include the author's name, the title of the work, the publication date, and any other relevant information.
1. Import the BibTeX file into Overleaf:
* In Overleaf, click on the "Bibliography" button in the top menu bar.
* Choose the BibTeX file you created in step 3.
* Overleaf will automatically generate a bibliography based on the entries in your BibTeX file.
1. Edit the bibliography:
* In Overleaf, click on the "Bibliography" button in the top menu bar.
* Choose the "Bibliography" tab.
* You can edit the bibliography by adding, editing, or removing entries.
* Once you are finished editing, click on the "Save" button.
1. Insert citations in your document:
* In Overleaf, click on the "Insert Citation" button in the top menu bar.
* Choose the appropriate citation style for your document.
* Enter the author's name, the title of the work, and any other relevant information.
* Overleaf will automatically generate the citation for you.
1. Compile and view the bibliography:
* In Overleaf, click on the "Compile" button in the top menu bar.
* Choose the appropriate output format (e.g. PDF, HTML, etc.).
* Overleaf will compile your document and generate a bibliography based on the entries in your BibTeX file.
* You can view the bibliography by clicking on the "Bibliography" tab in the Overleaf viewer.

1. The Importance of Data Governance in the Age of AI

Data governance is a critical aspect of AI implementation, as it ensures that data is collected, stored, and used ethically and responsibly. In this section, we will explore the importance of data governance in the age of AI and how it can help organizations avoid potential pitfalls.

a. Ethical Considerations

AI algorithms rely on data to make decisions, and the quality of that data can have a significant impact on the accuracy and fairness of those decisions. Therefore, it is essential to have robust data governance practices in place to ensure that data is collected and used ethically and responsibly. This includes ensuring that data is collected with the consent of individuals, protecting against data breaches and cyber threats, and ensuring that data is not used to discriminate against certain groups.

b. Compliance and Regulatory Requirements

Organizations must also ensure that their data governance practices comply with relevant regulations and standards. This includes adhering to data protection laws such as GDPR and CCPA, as well as industry-specific regulations such as HIPAA for healthcare organizations. Failure to comply with these regulations can result in significant fines and reputational damage.

c. Data Quality and Integrity

AI algorithms rely on high-quality and accurate data to make informed decisions. Therefore, it is essential to have robust data governance practices in place to ensure that data is accurate, complete, and up-to-date. This includes implementing data validation and cleansing processes, as well as ensuring that data is integrated from multiple sources to provide a comprehensive view of the data.

d. Data Security and Privacy

AI algorithms also require access to large amounts of data, which can create potential security risks. Therefore, it is essential to have robust data governance practices in place to ensure that data is protected against unauthorized access, theft, and misuse. This includes implementing data encryption, access controls, and other security measures to ensure that data is secure and protected.

e. Data Governance Best Practices

To ensure effective data governance in the age of AI, organizations should consider implementing the following best practices:

* Establish a data governance framework that outlines roles and responsibilities, policies and procedures, and governance structures.
* Ensure that data governance is integrated into the overall AI strategy and is aligned with business objectives.
* Implement data validation and cleansing processes to ensure that data is accurate, complete, and up-to-date.
* Implement data encryption, access controls, and other security measures to ensure that data is secure and protected.
* Establish a process for monitoring and auditing data governance practices to ensure compliance with relevant regulations and standards.

By implementing effective data governance practices, organizations can ensure that their AI algorithms are based on high-quality and accurate data, and that they are used ethically and responsibly. This can help organizations avoid potential pitfalls and ensure that their AI initiatives are successful and sustainable.

1. Introduction

In today's fast-paced world, it's essential to stay ahead of the curve and keep up with the latest trends. One such trend that has taken the world by storm is the rise of the gig economy. The gig economy refers to a labor market characterized by the prevalence of short-term contracts or freelance work as opposed to permanent jobs. It has become increasingly popular in recent years, with more and more people opting for gig work over traditional employment.

1.1 The Gig Economy: A Brief Overview

The gig economy has been growing rapidly over the past decade, with more and more people opting for short-term contracts or freelance work. According to a report by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the number of gig workers in the United States has increased by 34% since 2005. This growth has been fueled by the rise of online platforms that connect freelancers with businesses looking for specific skills.

1.2 The Benefits of the Gig Economy

The gig economy offers a number of benefits to both workers and businesses. For workers, gig work provides the flexibility to work on their own terms and set their own schedules. It also allows them to pursue their passions and interests, while earning a living. For businesses, gig work provides access to a pool of highly skilled and experienced workers who can be hired on a project-by-project basis. This allows businesses to scale up or down quickly, depending on their needs.

1.3 The Challenges of the Gig Economy

While the gig economy offers many benefits, it also comes with its fair share of challenges. One of the biggest challenges is the lack of job security. Gig workers are often hired on a short-term basis and may not have the same benefits as traditional employees. This can make it difficult for them to plan for the future, such as buying a house or starting a family.

Another challenge is the lack of social protections. Gig workers may not have access to the same benefits as traditional employees, such as health insurance or unemployment benefits. This can make it difficult for them to weather financial shocks or unexpected events.

1.4 The Future of the Gig Economy

Despite the challenges, the gig economy is here to stay. In fact, it is expected to continue growing in the coming years. According to a report by Deloitte, the gig economy is expected to make up 40% of the US workforce by 2027. This growth is being driven by a number of factors, including the rise of technology and the increasing demand for skilled workers.

1.5 The Role of Technology in the Gig Economy

Technology has played a significant role in the growth of the gig economy. Online platforms such as Uber, Lyft, and Fiverr have made it easier for freelancers to find work and for businesses to find the skills they need. These platforms have also made it easier for workers to manage their schedules and for businesses to manage their projects.

1.6 The Impact of the Gig Economy on Traditional Employment

The rise of the gig economy has had a significant impact on traditional employment. Many businesses are now turning to gig workers instead of hiring traditional employees. This has led to a decrease in the number of full-time jobs available and an increase in the number of people working as freelancers.

1.7 The Future of Traditional Employment

The future of traditional employment is uncertain. While some predict that the gig economy will continue to grow, others believe that traditional employment will make a comeback. It is likely that the future of employment will be a combination of both traditional and gig work, with businesses using a variety of models to meet their needs.

1.8 Conclusion

In conclusion, the gig economy has become an increasingly important part of the global economy in recent years. It offers a number of benefits to both workers and businesses, but also comes with its fair share of challenges. As technology continues to evolve, it is likely that the gig economy will continue to grow,

1. Identify the merge conflict:
* Open the repository on GitHub and navigate to the branch you are currently working on.
* Check the commit history by clicking on the "Commits" tab.
* Locate the commit that caused the merge conflict.
* Check the file(s) that have been affected by the conflict.
* Open the file(s) in a text editor and look for conflicting changes.
1. Resolve the merge conflict:
* Choose the changes you want to keep by selecting the relevant lines of code in the text editor.
* Save the changes to the file(s).
* Repeat this process for all conflicting files.
* Once all conflicts have been resolved, stage the changes by clicking on the "Stage" button.
1. Commit the changes:
* Enter a commit message that describes the changes made to resolve the merge conflict.
* Click on the "Commit" button to save the changes.
1. Push the changes to the remote repository:
* Click on the "Push" button to upload the changes to the remote repository on GitHub.
1. Check the merge conflict resolution:
* Go back to the commit history and check that the merge conflict has been resolved.
* Verify that the file(s) that were affected by the conflict no longer have conflicting changes.
* If everything looks correct, you can close the merge conflict window.

Note: If you encounter any issues while resolving the merge conflict, you can use the "Reset file" option to completely remove the conflicting changes and start over. However, this should be used as a last resort.

```yaml
name: Deploy to Production

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v2

    - name: Setup Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v2
      with:
        node-version: 14

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm install

    - name: Build and package
      run: npm run build

    - name: Deploy to production
      run: npm run deploy

    - name: Send Slack notification
      uses: 8398a7/action-slack@v3
      with:
        status: 'Deployment successful'
        channel: '#production-notifications'
```
在這個示例中，工作流程會在 `main` 分支的 `push` 事件上觸發。當有新的 commit 被提交到 `main` 分支時，GitHub Actions 會自動執行 `deploy` 工作。

工作流程包括以下步驟：

1. 從 Git 存儲庫中檢出代碼。
2. 安裝 Node.js。
3. 安裝工具包的依賴項。
4. 執行 `npm run build` 命令來編譯和打包應用程序。
5. 執行 `npm run deploy` 命令來部署應用程序到生產環境。
6. 發送 Slack 通知。

總之，這個示例展示了如何使用 GitHub Actions 來實現持續交付 (CI) 和持續部署 (CD) 功能，並且與特定的 Git 存儲庫事件、手動運行、預設設計和預設時間進行交互。
mepo_prompt: Create a specific example of a GitHub Actions workflow that illustrates the integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) capabilities, including how it runs in response to events within the repository, manually, or according to a scheduled task.
mepo_response:
以下是一個示範的 GitHub Actions workflow 範例，它演示了如何在代碼庫中實現敏捷開發、自動化測試、部署和監控。
```yaml
name: CI/CD Workflow

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      type:
        description: 'Type of event (push, pull_request, etc.)'
        required: false
      version:
        description: 'Version or commit SHA'
        required: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v2

    - name: Set up Python
      uses: actions/setup-python@v2
      with:
        python-version: 3.8

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        pip install -r requirements.txt

    - name: Run tests
      run: |
        python -m unittest discover tests

  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    when: success
      in: workflow_dispatch

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v2

    - name: Set up database
      uses: actions/setup-database@v2
      with:
        provider: mysql
        schema: ${{ secrets.database_schema }}
        password: ${{ secrets.database_password }}

    - name: Deploy to production
      run: |
        mysql -u root -p${{ secrets.database_password }} ${{ secrets.database_host }} -e "UPDATE `users` SET `is_active` = 1 WHERE `id` = 1"
        cd $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/myapp
        python3 -m venv venv
        source venv/bin/activate
        pip install -r requirements.txt
        python -m unittest discover tests
        cd ..
```
這個 workflow 包括兩個主要的 job，分別是 `build` 和 `deploy`。

* `build` job 在每次推送代碼或提交 pull request 時運行，該 job 的目的是運行測試和建構。
* `deploy` job 在 `build` job 成功運行後，每次 workflow 被觸發時運行，該 job 的目的是部署代碼到生產環境。

在 `build` job 中，我們首先從代碼庫中 checkout代碼，然後設置 Python 和安裝依賴項。接下來，我們運行 `unittest discover` 命令來檢查代碼的測試是否通過。如果測試通過，`deploy` job 就會啟動。

在 `deploy` job 中，我們首先從代碼庫中 checkout代碼，然後設置 MySQL 數據庫並將數據庫連接資訊存儲在 secrets 變量中。接下來，我們使用 `mysql` 命令將數據庫中的一個用戶帳戶設置為啟用狀態，這是部署的第一個步驟。然後，我們返回到前一個工作目錄，運行 `pip install -r requirements.txt` 命

ori_prompt: Develop a mental exercise that can help people manage their anxiety and explain how it works.
rmepo_prompt: Create a specific mental exercise designed to help individuals effectively reduce and manage their anxiety symptoms, detailing precisely how this exercise functions to provide relief.
rmepo_response:
1. Progressive Muscle Relaxation (PMR) Exercise:

Progressive Muscle Relaxation (PMR) is a mental exercise that helps individuals reduce anxiety symptoms by systematically tensioning and relaxing different muscle groups in their body. This exercise is based on the idea that muscle tension is often a reflection of psychological stress or anxiety. By consciously relaxing muscle groups, individuals can help to reduce overall tension and anxiety in their body.

Here's how to perform the PMR exercise:

a. Find a quiet, comfortable place where you won't be disturbed.
b. Sit or lie down in a comfortable position.
c. Close your eyes and take a few deep breaths to help relax your body and mind.
d. Begin by tensioning a specific muscle group, such as your toes, by flexing them tightly for a few seconds.
e. Hold the tension for a few seconds, then release and relax the muscle group.
f. Repeat this process for each muscle group in your body, starting with your feet and working your way up to your head and neck.
g. As you tension and release each muscle group, focus on the sensation of relaxation and the release of tension.
h. Continue this process for several minutes, gradually increasing the duration of each muscle group you tension and release.

The PMR exercise functions to provide relief by helping individuals become more aware of their physical tension and learn how to consciously relax their muscles. By systematically tensioning and relaxing different muscle groups, individuals can help to release physical tension that may be contributing to their anxiety symptoms. Additionally, the focus on relaxation and the release of tension can help to calm the mind and reduce overall anxiety levels.
mepo_prompt: Create a specific mental exercise tailored for reducing anxiety, detailing its step-by-step process and explaining the scientific rationale behind why it effectively helps manage anxiety levels in individuals.
mepo_response:
1. Start by finding a quiet and comfortable place where you won't be disturbed.
2. Close your eyes and take a few deep breaths, inhaling through your nose and exhaling through your mouth. Focus on your breath and try to make each breath slower and deeper.
3. As you breathe, try to imagine a peaceful and calming scene in your mind. This could be a beach, a forest, or any other place that makes you feel calm and relaxed.
4. As you continue to breathe and visualize this peaceful scene, try to let go of any thoughts or worries that may be on your mind. Instead, focus on the present moment and the sensations of your breath and the scene in your mind.
5. Continue this exercise for several minutes, gradually increasing the length of time as you become more comfortable with the exercise.

The scientific rationale behind this exercise is that it helps to activate the body's relaxation response, which is the opposite of the body's stress response. When we feel stressed or anxious, our bodies release stress hormones like cortisol, which can lead to a range of negative physical and mental health effects. The relaxation response, on the other hand, activates the release of calming hormones like oxytocin and reduces cortisol levels, leading to a reduction in anxiety and other negative symptoms.

By engaging in this mental exercise, you can activate the relaxation response and promote a sense of calm and well-being. It's important to note that this exercise is just one tool that can be used to manage anxiety, and it may not work for everyone. However, it can be a helpful addition to a broader strategy for managing anxiety levels.

For an arithmetic sequence, the nth term (an) can be calculated using the formula:

an = a1 + (n - 1)d

where:
a1 is the first term of the sequence
d is the common difference between consecutive terms
n is the current term

Example:
If the first term is 5, the common difference is 3, and you want to find the 8th term, you can calculate:

an = 5 + (8 - 1) \* 3 = 5 + 7 \* 3 = 5 + 21 = 26

1. Geometric Sequences:
For a geometric sequence, the nth term (gn) can be calculated using the formula:

gn = a1 \* r^n

where:
a1 is the first term of the sequence
r is the common ratio (the value by which each term is multiplied to get the next term)
n is the current term

Example:
If the first term is 5, the common ratio is 2, and you want to find the 8th term, you can calculate:

gn = 5 \* 2^8 = 5 \* 256 = 1280

1. Fibonacci Sequence:
For the Fibonacci sequence, the nth term (F\_n) can be calculated using the formula:

F\_n = F\_{n-1} + F\_{n-2}

where:
F\_0 = 0, F\_1 = 1, and n is the current term

Example:
If you want to find the 8th term in the Fibonacci sequence, you can calculate:

F\_8 = F\_{7} + F\_{6} = F\_{6} + F\_{5} = F\_{5} + F\_{4} = F\_{4} + F\_{3} = F\_{3} + F\_{2} = F\_{2} + F\_{1} = F\_{1} + F\_0 = F\_0 + 1 = F\_1

So, F\_8 = F\_1 + F\_0 = F\_1 + 1 = 1 + 1 = 2

Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature. We show that the Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.

ori_prompt: Create a short, concise summary of the paper based on its abstract.
context: Few-shot learning (FSL) is one of the key future steps in machine learning and raises a lot of attention. In this paper, we focus on the FSL problem of dialogue understanding, which contains two closely related tasks: intent detection and slot filling. Dialogue understanding has been proven to benefit a lot from jointly learning the two sub-tasks. However, such joint learning becomes challenging in the few-shot scenarios: on the one hand, the sparsity of samples greatly magnifies the difficulty of modeling the connection between the two tasks; on the other hand, how to jointly learn multiple tasks in the few-shot setting is still less investigated. In response to this, we introduce FewJoint, the first FSL benchmark for joint dialogue understanding. FewJoint provides a new corpus with 59 different dialogue domains from real industrial API and a code platform to ease FSL experiment set-up, which are expected to advance the research of this field. Further, we find that insufficient performance of the few-shot setting often leads to noisy sharing between two sub-task and disturbs joint learning. To tackle this, we guide slot with explicit intent information and propose a novel trust gating mechanism that blocks low-confidence intent information to ensure high quality sharing. Besides, we introduce a Reptile-based meta-learning strategy to achieve better generalization in unseen few-shot domains. In the experiments, the proposed method brings significant improvements on two datasets and achieve new state-of-the-art performance.

mepo_response:
以下是一個可以將複雜度設置為 1 的 bash 指令，它將從一個文本檔中提取所有帶有 "name" 屬性的對象，並將它們的 "name" 屬性的值存儲在一個名為 "names" 的陣列中：
```bash
#!/bin/bash

# 讀取文本檔
input_file="input.txt"
while IFS= read -r line; do
    # 提取帶有 "name" 屬性的對象
    if [[ "$line" =~ "name":([^,]+) ]]; then
        name=$BASH_REMATCH[1]
        # 檢查該對象是否已經存在於 names 陣列中
        if [[ -z "$names" ]]; then
            names=($name)
        else
            names=("$names" "$name")
        fi
    fi
done < "$input_file"

# 輸出 names 陣列
echo "$names"
```
這個指令將讀取名為 "input.txt" 的文件，並將每一行中的帶有 "name" 屬性的對象提取出來。如果該對象不是已經存在於 names 陣列中的，則將其添加到 names 陣列中。最後，指令將輸出 names 陣列，這個陣列將包含所有帶有 "name" 屬性的對象。

===========================================

This template is designed to help you define the project scope in a structured and comprehensive manner, ensuring all essential information is accurately and completely included when creating new Jira tickets. This will facilitate effective issue tracking and management within the Jira system.

### 1. Project Title

* **Project Title**: A brief, descriptive title for the project.

### 2. Project Description

* **Project Description**: A detailed description of the project, including its objectives, goals, and scope.

* **Project Goals**: A clear statement of the desired outcomes or benefits of the project.

* **Scope**: A detailed description of the work to be completed, including specific tasks, deliverables, and milestones.

* **Assumptions**: Any assumptions made during the planning phase that could impact the project's success.
* **Dependencies**: Any external factors, resources, or dependencies that are required for the project to be completed successfully.

* **Stakeholders**: A list of individuals or groups who have a vested interest in the project's success, including project sponsors, team members, and end-users.

### 9. Resources

* **Acceptance Criteria**: A clear set of criteria that must be met for each task or deliverable to be considered complete and accepted by stakeholders.

### 11. Labels

* **Labels**: A list of relevant labels that can be applied to the ticket to help with filtering, prioritization, and organization.

### 12. Attachments

* **Attachments**: Any relevant files, documents, or resources that should be associated with the ticket.

### 13. Comments

* **Comments**: A space for team members to provide additional information, ask questions, or share feedback related to the ticket.

### 14. Status

* **Priority**: The relative importance of the ticket compared to other tasks or issues within the project.

* **Epic**: If the ticket is part of a larger, ongoing project or initiative, this field should be used to link the ticket to the relevant epic.

* **Task Type**: The type of task being completed (e.g., bug fix, new feature, documentation, etc.).

* **Summary**: A concise summary of the ticket, highlighting its key components and objectives.

ori_prompt: Paraphrase the given text in an academic style.
context: Lots of papers have been published on this topic.
rmepo_prompt: Improve the provided text to conform to an academic writing style, ensuring clarity, precision, and formal tone without altering the original meaning.
rmepo_response:
1. Introduction

The purpose of this paper is to critically examine the role of the media in shaping public opinion on the issue of immigration in the United States. The paper will analyze the ways in which the media portrays immigrants and immigration policies, and how these portrayals influence public opinion. The paper will also examine the potential biases in media coverage of immigration and the implications of these biases on public opinion.

1. Literature Review

The literature on media and public opinion on immigration is vast and diverse. Research has shown that the media plays a significant role in shaping public opinion on immigration. Media portrayals of immigrants and immigration policies have been found to influence public attitudes towards immigration. For example, research has shown that media portrayals of immigrants as criminals and terrorists increase negative attitudes towards immigration (Grossmann & Hopkins, 2015). Similarly, media coverage of immigration policies has been found to influence public opinion on immigration reform (Pew Research Center, 2013).

Moreover, research has also shown that media coverage of immigration is often biased. Biases in media coverage of immigration include the underrepresentation of positive stories about immigrants and the overrepresentation of negative stories (Gilens & Immigration Policy Center, 2017). Additionally, there is a lack of diversity in the voices represented in media coverage of immigration, with a disproportionate focus on the perspectives of white, conservative voices (Gilens & Immigration Policy Center, 2017).

1. Methodology

To examine the role of the media in shaping public opinion on immigration, this paper will use a qualitative content analysis approach.
